result.title: Learning Non-Gaussian SEMs with Conditional Risk, and Why the Direction of Recursion Matters
result.summary: Variance-based methods recover a Gaussian linear structural equation model (SEM) with equal or suitably constrained error variances, either by recursively identifying the source nodes with smallest conditional variance (top-down method) or sink nodes with highest conditional variance (bottom-up method). We show that the use of conditional variance is incidental: replacing it with the conditional risk, i.e., the minimal expected loss of linear prediction under the negative log-likelihood of the noise distribution, extends both methods to non-Gaussian noise. Existing methods are the least-squares special case. This yields two main results. First, exploiting the noise distribution improves structure recovery: the matched-loss procedures recover the SEM more accurately than their least-squares counterparts and the LiNGAM methods, which are designed for non-Gaussianity. Second, the two methods, interchangeable in the Gaussian setting, separate under non-Gaussian noise: the top-down method is correct for every noise density with finite differential entropy, whereas the bottom-up method requires a regularity condition and can fail without it, for instance under mean-zero exponential or Cauchy noise. Simulations confirm both results.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究非高斯线性结构方程模型的结构识别，用「条件风险」（噪声分布下线性预测的最小期望损失）替代条件方差，把自顶向下与自底向上两种递归识别方法推广到非高斯噪声，并证明二者在非高斯下不再等价：top-down 在有限微分熵下即正确，bottom-up 需额外正则条件且可能失效，模拟予以验证。
